title: Trump Impeached a Second Time for Incitement
description_short: Trump Impeached a Second Time for Incitement
description_medium: On January 13, 2021, the House impeached Trump for “incitement of insurrection” related to the January 6 attack on the Capitol. The vote was 232–197, with all Democrats and ten Republicans supporting impeachment. It made Trump the first U.S. president impeached twice. The House’s action charged him; the Senate later held a trial and acquitted him, so impeachment was not a criminal conviction or removal from office.
description_long: The House of Representatives impeached President Donald Trump for a second time on January 13, 2021, approving an article charging “incitement of insurrection” in connection with the January 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol. The House Clerk recorded a 232–197 vote, with ten Republicans joining all voting Democrats in support. The action made Trump the only U.S. president to be impeached twice. Impeachment is a charge brought by the House, not a criminal conviction; the Senate later held a trial and did not reach the two-thirds vote required to convict. Trump therefore remained in office until the end of his term and was acquitted by the Senate. The record captures the House vote and charge, while the Senate result supplies the constitutional outcome. Describing both stages avoids treating the impeachment itself as a removal or as proof of a criminal offense. The vote was a major institutional response to the attack and to Trump’s conduct as characterized in the article of impeachment.
